panels.title: z-score + position state (per pair / variant)
panels.description: Combined view: z-score lines (left scale) plus per-variant position-state bars overlaid at fixed Y levels (canary a=3.5, main a=3.0, main b=2.5, main c=2.0). Position bars are `(pairtrade_has_position == 1) * Y_offset` rendered as thick step lines so the same panel timeline aligns z and position on identical x-pixels.

panels.title: z-score divergence: Frankfurt A/B/C - canary (per variant)
panels.description: Frankfurt main z minus Frankfurt canary z, broadcast on pair (group_left) so canary's single series compares against each of A/B/C. Structural drift is expected per bot-strategy#410 (separate process, independent WS bar close); the panel is a direction indicator for binary-regression detection rather than a 'should be 0' alert. Requires canary added to Alloy scrape with instance="debot-frankfurt-canary".

panels.title: Relative beta_gap = |beta_s - beta_l| / beta_eff (gate 0.30)
panels.description: Relative beta divergence = |beta_s - beta_l| / beta_eff. This is the value the entry filter compares against `beta_divergence_max` (default 0.30) — exceeding the red line hard-blocks entries, and `beta_gap_entry_z_scale` linearly raises the entry-z threshold even below it. Replaces the prior `pairtrade_beta_divergence` plot which showed the absolute gap on the same threshold line and was not comparable to the gate.

panels.title: Position age (seconds, > 0 only while in position)
Time since last trade (seconds, -1 before first trade)
Close gross PnL — per close (bps of entry notional)
panels.description: Per-close gross PnL (price moves only, fees+funding excluded) normalized by entry notional, plotted as scatter (1 point ≈ 1 close). pairtrade closes ~1-2/day per variant; the prior heatmap form (pairtrade#35) was too sparse to show signal. Replaced per bot-strategy#420. Source for #306 BT/live gap analysis. (#314 Group 4-A)

panels.title: Per-leg slippage p50/p90 (bps, by order_type)
panels.description: Median + 90th-percentile slippage vs decision-time reference price, signed positive = cost. post_only fills typically hover near 0; taker fills are the adverse tail #306 cares about. (#314 Group 4-B/B-2, pairtrade#38/#42)

panels.title: Canary restart events (24h count via process_start change)
panels.description: bot-strategy#412 signal #1. `changes(pairtrade_process_start_timestamp_seconds[24h])` = number of restarts in the last 24h. Canary auto-restarts on each CI deploy (#376), so the typical level is 1-3/day. Spikes above 5/day indicate either CI churn or a `Restart=on-failure` loop (the latter is the binary-regression signal). Unexpected-exit details (SIGKILL, timeout) are surfaced separately by the error-watch workflow (#168) as auto-issues.

panels.title: Canary / main-A trade rate ratio (24h)
panels.description: bot-strategy#412 signal #5 supplement. Ratio of canary trade count to main A trade count (`pairtrade_close_gross_pnl_bps_count`). Target >= 2.0 per #376 (canary entry_z=1.0 vs main A 1.5 → ~2-3x). Below 1.5 means canary stopped trading at its expected aggressive pace, e.g. a binary that silently breaks entry logic.

panels.title: Canary per-leg slippage p50/p95 — entry (bps)
panels.description: bot-strategy#412 signal #4. Canary-only view of `pairtrade_leg_slippage_bps` for the entry leg, split by order_type (post_only vs taker). Positive bps = cost (paid more than reference). Panel 17 above mixes canary into the global `variant!=""` aggregate; this panel isolates the canary path so binary regression in fill quality is visible. Baseline + threshold tuning is bot-strategy#412 Stage B/C (~2026-05-21 → 2026-05-28).

panels.title: Canary per-leg slippage p50/p95 — exit (bps)
panels.description: bot-strategy#412 signal #4, exit-leg companion to panel 23. Exit-side slippage is the leg-sync tail that pairtrade#23 / bot-strategy#258 cared about — for canary the regression signal is the same shape as entry but on the exit path.

panels.title: Canary close gross PnL — per close (bps of entry notional)
panels.description: bot-strategy#412 signal #5. Canary-only per-close gross PnL (fees+funding excluded), filtered to instance=debot-frankfurt-canary. Plotted as scatter (1 point ≈ 1 close); the prior heatmap form was too sparse for canary's trade cadence. A binary that breaks position sizing / exit logic shifts the mode away from zero or fattens the loss tail. Replaced per bot-strategy#420.

panels.title: [Tokyo Extended] z-score + position state (per pair / variant)
panels.description: Combined view: z-score line plus position-state bar at Y=3.0 (`pairtrade_has_position == 1` rendered as a thick step line). Tokyo Extended is single-variant so there is one z line and one position bar.

panels.title: [Tokyo Extended] Relative beta_gap = |beta_s - beta_l| / beta_eff (gate 0.30)
panels.description: Relative beta divergence = |beta_s - beta_l| / beta_eff. This is the value the entry filter compares against `beta_divergence_max` (default 0.30) — exceeding the red line hard-blocks entries, and `beta_gap_entry_z_scale` linearly raises the entry-z threshold even below it. Replaces the prior `pairtrade_beta_divergence` plot which showed the absolute gap on the same threshold line and was not comparable to the gate.

panels.title: [Tokyo Extended] Position age (seconds, > 0 only while in position)
[Tokyo Extended] Time since last trade (seconds, -1 before first trade)
[Tokyo Extended] Close gross PnL — per close (bps of entry notional)
panels.description: Per-close gross PnL (price moves only, fees+funding excluded) normalized by entry notional, plotted as scatter (1 point ≈ 1 close). pairtrade closes ~1-2/day per variant; the prior heatmap form (pairtrade#35) was too sparse to show signal. Replaced per bot-strategy#420. Source for #306 BT/live gap analysis. (#314 Group 4-A) Tokyo Extended uses [$__range] (vs Frankfurt [$__rate_interval]) so the mean survives the panel window at single-bot, sub-1-trade/h cadence.

panels.title: [Tokyo Extended] Slippage fill samples (count by order_type)
panels.description: Cumulative fill-event count over the panel window, broken down by order_type (post_only vs taker). Replaces the Frankfurt-style p50/p90 view because Extended single-bot cadence (~1 trade/day) gives too few samples to compute meaningful quantiles per scrape interval. Revisit p50/p90 once trade density rises. (#314)

panels.title: [Tokyo Extended] Fee samples (count by leg)
panels.description: Cumulative fee-event count over the panel window, broken down by leg (entry vs exit). Confirms fee samples are reaching the histogram. p50/p90 replaced because single-bot cadence floors rate() to zero outside the scrape window. (#314)

panels.title: [Tokyo Extended] Fill latency samples (count by leg)
panels.description: Cumulative fill-latency sample count over the panel window, by leg. p50/p90 replaced for the same reason as the slippage/fee panels — quantiles need denser samples than Extended currently produces. (#314)

panels.title: Maintenance / degraded windows (#427)
panels.description: 1 when the per-tick gate observes maintenance_status() != None on the venue connector. Captures both RSS-announced Lighter maintenance (`upcoming_or_active`) and observed-degraded mode from the OutageDetector (`degraded_observed`, latched on 6 REST/WS/read_mid failures in 60s, cleared on 3 consecutive successes). xvenue-arb additionally folds in Extended's announced maintenance. Visualises the exact windows during which entries are blocked and error-watch is suppressed.

panels.title: Entry rejects breakdown (24h, by gate) — Frankfurt + Tokyo Lighter
panels.description: Stacked area of `increase(pairtrade_entry_reject_total[24h])` summed over the Frankfurt + Tokyo Lighter pairtrade fleet, broken down by the gate that fired. Use this to see which filter is responsible for blocked entries — especially when the live trade rate looks low. Common reasons in production: `z_below_threshold` (most cycles' z is just under the dynamic threshold; influenced by `beta_gap_entry_z_scale`), `beta_divergence` (hard gate at `beta_divergence_max=0.30`), `beta_min` (hedge leg too small), `mtf` (multi-timeframe z-confluence). Added for bot-strategy#355 Round-4 follow-up.

panels.title: Kalman beta uncertainty (sqrt(P)) — calibration view
panels.description: `pairtrade_beta_uncertainty` = sqrt of the Kalman filter's posterior variance. This is the rigorous 1-sigma uncertainty of the current beta estimate; it dominates the beta_s/beta_l divergence proxy used today. Phase 1 of bot-strategy#462: gauge only — we observe the distribution for 1-2 weeks across calm and unstable periods, then set `beta_uncertainty_max` from the calibration data and flip the gate. Frankfurt + Tokyo Lighter shown; Tokyo Extended excluded (single-bot, different cadence).

panels.title: Re-hedge needed events (24h, per variant) — #463 Phase 1
panels.description: `increase(pairtrade_rehedge_needed_total[24h])` per Frankfurt variant. Phase 1 is **detection only** — these events fire when `|β_now − β_entry| / β_entry ≥ rehedge_drift_threshold_pct` and the cool-down + min-notional floors allow firing, but no order is placed. Use this to calibrate the three thresholds (`rehedge_drift_threshold_pct`, `rehedge_cooldown_secs`, `rehedge_min_qty_notional_usd`) before enabling Phase 2's actual re-hedge. Default config has the feature disabled (threshold=0.0) so this panel shows 0 until an operator opts in.

panels.title: Strategy step duration p50 / p99
panels.description: Engine-wide wall-clock duration of Strategy::step(). Compare Frankfurt main/canary and Tokyo Extended; p99 tail is the regression signal tracked by bot-strategy#417.

panels.title: Capital / leverage config drift
panels.description: Resolved runtime config per host and variant. Differences are expected only when explicitly planned; unexpected changes indicate environment/YAML drift (bot-strategy#314 Group 7).
